headline: xAI bundles Grok, Cursor and X Premium into one subscription
dek: The X Subscription replaces separate plans with one package and a shared usage pool, according to xAI and Engadget.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Three plans become one
body: On October 12, xAI launched The X Subscription, a single plan that bundles the Grok chat app, the Grok Bot assistant, the Cursor coding tool and paid X Premium features (xAI, Engadget).
It replaces the separate subscriptions with one usage pool shared between the chatbot and Cursor. Unused allowance in one app carries over to the other (Engadget).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Four paid tiers, plus a free one
s3.body: According to Engadget, the entry tier, Plus, costs $8 a month. The rest follow Cursor's existing per-seat team pricing (xAI, Engadget).

points.t: Adds Grok Bot, the latest Grok models and image and video generation (Engadget).
Includes all that plus priority access to Grok models at peak times (Engadget).
Gives earliest access to products and models, with 20 times the usage of Plus (Engadget).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Fewer bills for people using both
body: For developers and companies paying for both Grok and Cursor, a shared pool can mean fewer subscriptions to track. The actual savings depend on how much each product gets used (Engadget).
xAI says every paid tier delivers more usage per dollar than the plan it replaces.

stat.cap: a month, from Plus to Ultra

items.t: The plan is open to new customers and rolls out to everyone globally in the coming days (xAI).
They can keep their plan or switch and get a prorated refund for unused time (xAI, Engadget).
xAI says it will give notice before moving people who do not switch, but set no date (xAI).

caption.hook: xAI folded Grok, Cursor and X Premium into one subscription, from $8 to $200 a month.
body: According to xAI, the plan replaces the separate subscriptions and shares one usage pool between the chatbot and Cursor, the coding tool the company acquired in August (Engadget). Unused allowance in one app carries over to the other.

Current subscribers can keep their plan or switch with a prorated refund (xAI, Engadget). Team plans add single sign-on, admin controls and SOC 2 compliance. xAI says it will give notice before moving people who do not switch, but set no date.
